channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President to Remain in Office During Election Campaign, Speaker Says
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov will not step down during the upcoming election campaign, according to Parliament Speaker Marlen Mamataliev. Current legislation does not require the president to suspend duties while running for office. Mamataliev confirmed all government branches will continue to function normally.

item.title: SCO Summit and State Visits Underway in Bishkek, Security Tightened
item.description: Bishkek is hosting the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit and official state visits on August 31 and September 1, expecting 21 presidents and prime ministers. Unprecedented security measures are in place. The summit marks the SCO's 25th anniversary. China's President Xi Jinping held talks with Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov.

item.title: Togo's Prime Minister arrives in Kyrgyzstan for working visit and SCO meeting
item.description: Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, Chairman of the Council of Ministers of Togo, has arrived in Kyrgyzstan for a working visit. He will attend the high-level SCO Plus meeting and the opening ceremony of the VI World Nomad Games. Kyrgyzstan currently chairs the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.

item.title: First direct flight from Dushanbe to Minsk welcomed with ceremony
item.description: The first direct flight from Dushanbe by Somon Air landed in Minsk on August 29, marking the opening of a new air route. The aircraft was met with a traditional water arch and Belarusian bread, symbolizing hospitality.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan-China cooperation enters new 'golden period', says President Japarov
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov stated that Kyrgyzstan-China relations have reached a historically high level and entered a new, golden period of development. He thanked Chinese President Xi Jinping for his state visit during the SCO summit.

item.title: Central Asia's Great Purge: Arrests and Fate of Children Detailed
item.description: Documents reveal plans for the repression of 224,400 individuals across Central Asia. Uzbekistan SSR was slated to condemn 4,750 people, with 750 in the first category and 4,000 in the second, according to NKVD data.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Departs for SCO Summit in Bishkek
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon has traveled to Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit. He was seen off at Dushanbe International Airport by high-ranking officials, including parliamentary leaders and the Prime Minister.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Mining Companies Can Recalculate Purchases Due to Weak Tenge
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Industry and Construction allows solid mineral mining companies to adjust purchase costs based on the tenge's exchange rate. This applies to contracts before signing and during payment, with suppliers needing to provide detailed cost calculations.

item.title: Russia's Defense Ministry announces preparations for large-scale strikes on Ukraine's energy sector
item.description: The Russian Armed Forces are preparing massive strikes on Ukrainian energy facilities, according to the Russian Ministry of Defense. The ministry stated these strikes are a response to alleged Ukrainian attacks on Russian civilian infrastructure and energy complex. This announcement follows reports of Ukrainian drone attacks impacting Russian oil refineries and energy infrastructure, leading to reduced gasoline production and fuel export restrictions.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India agree to introduce a 30-day visa-free regime for mutual travel
item.description: Uzbekistan and India have signed agreements to expand tourism cooperation, including a 30-day visa-free regime for citizens of both countries. The agreements were reached during high-level talks between Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The cooperation program for 2026-2028 also includes joint cultural events and the development of new tourist routes to increase mutual tourist flow.

item.title: Kazakhstan spent hundreds of billions of tenge on energy grid repairs, but wear and tear has barely decreased
item.description: Kazakhstan allocated 384 billion tenge for energy infrastructure repairs in 2026, a 9% increase from the previous year. However, these investments will only slightly reduce network wear, according to Ranking.kz. While repairs on power plants and transmission lines are progressing, heat networks face delays. Despite significant spending, the wear on power plants will decrease from 53% to 52%, and on heat networks from 50% to 48%.

item.title: Uzbekistan's UN Resident Coordinator reflects on two years of changes, people, and opportunities, highlighting climate change impacts
item.description: Akiko Fujii, the UN Resident Coordinator in Uzbekistan, reflects on her two years in the country, noting the significance of the end of the 'chilla' heat period. She highlights the pressing issue of climate change in Uzbekistan, where over 25% of land is degraded and nearly 45% is at risk of desertification. Fujii emphasizes that climate change is a daily reality, particularly concerning given that 80% of the country's water resources are imported.

item.title: Olzhas Bektenov Reappointed as Prime Minister of Kazakhstan
item.description: Olzhas Bektenov has been reappointed as the Prime Minister of Kazakhstan by the Kurultai, following a vote chaired by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. Bektenov, who has held the position since 2024, expressed gratitude for the trust and emphasized supporting the president's modernization initiatives.

item.title: Number of Entrepreneurs Grows in Tajikistan
item.description: Tajikistan saw a 4.3% increase in entrepreneurship subjects by July 1, 2026, totaling over 391,000, according to the State Committee on Investments. Financial support also rose, with over 6.3 billion somoni in loans granted in the first half of 2026, a 7.4% increase from the previous year.

item.title: Erlan Karin Appointed Vice President of Kazakhstan
item.description: Former State Secretary Erlan Karin has been appointed Vice President of Kazakhstan following a vote by the Kurultai, chaired by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. Tokayev praised Karin's extensive experience and contributions to the country's development, calling him a worthy candidate for the newly defined role.

item.title: US Strikes Iran, Tehran Targets US Bases in Jordan
item.description: US forces attacked missile launch sites on Iran's Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz on August 30. In response, Iran launched missile strikes against US military bases in Jordan, including King Hussein and Al-Azraq.

item.title: SCO Humanitarian Event Held in Bishkek Ahead of 2026 Summit
item.description: A humanitarian event for SCO countries was held in Bishkek on August 30, organized by China Media Group and Kyrgyzstan's National TV and Radio Broadcasting Corporation. Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov sent a congratulatory message, emphasizing the media's role in strengthening understanding.

item.title: Documentary 'In the Name of the Future' Marks SCO's 25th Anniversary
item.description: The documentary 'In the Name of the Future' highlights the achievements and significance of multilateral cooperation within the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation. It explores themes like artificial intelligence, infrastructure, agriculture, environmental protection, and humanitarian exchanges, showcasing joint efforts for regional progress.

item.title: Tashkent Bus Fares Must Be Paid Upon Boarding Starting September 1
item.description: Starting September 1, passengers on Tashkent buses operating under gross contract agreements must pay fares immediately upon boarding. Payment can be made via transport card, bank card, smartphone, or other contactless methods. Failure to pay will be considered fare evasion.

item.title: Uzbekistan discusses revised curriculum: what kind of graduate do we envision?
item.description: Uzbekistan is debating revised state education standards and curricula for general education schools. The discussion, limited to 15 days, focuses on the educational philosophy and alignment of competencies with goals. Experts and parents urge for a transparent, extended public discussion on the new standards and implementation mechanisms.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Decriminalizing Personal Drug Possession
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs proposes shifting responsibility for possessing, acquiring, transporting, manufacturing, and consuming small amounts of drugs for personal use from criminal to administrative offenses. Criminal liability will remain for drug trafficking, production for sale, and large quantities. This reform aims to address the high number of dismissed cases.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Appoints New Ambassador to Tajikistan
item.description: Nazarali Aripov has been appointed as the new Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Kyrgyzstan to Tajikistan. The decree was signed by Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov. Aripov replaces Erlan Abdildaev, who was previously released from this post and appointed Ambassador to Hungary.

item.title: UN Secretary-General António Guterres Arrives in Kyrgyzstan for SCO Summit
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres has arrived in Kyrgyzstan to participate in the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit. He was welcomed at Manas International Airport by the Minister of Economy and Commerce, Bakyt Sydykov. Guterres will attend the Council of Heads of State meeting in Bishkek.

item.title: 12 Uzbek children without parental care returned from Russia
item.description: Twelve underage Uzbek citizens, deprived of parental care or in difficult social situations, have been returned to Uzbekistan from various regions of Russia. The repatriation was a collaborative effort involving the Uzbek embassy, ministries of internal affairs and health, and the National Agency for Social Protection. This year, 38 children have been repatriated from Russia.

item.title: Uzbek President congratulates Kyrgyzstan on Independence Day
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev congratulated Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov and the people of Kyrgyzstan on Independence Day. Mirziyoyev noted Kyrgyzstan's economic and social growth under Japarov's leadership and highlighted the elevated bilateral relations to a "union level." He also emphasized the importance of regional cooperation and upcoming events.

item.title: Hong Kong banks may finance Tashkent-Samarkand toll road project
item.description: Hong Kong banks are considering financing the construction of the Tashkent-Samarkand toll road. The potential involvement of Hong Kong financial institutions was discussed by Uzbekistan's Transport Minister Ilkhom Makhkamov and the head of Hong Kong's "Belt and Road" Office, Nicholas Ho Lik-chi. Prospects for air travel and economic cooperation were also discussed.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Parliament Speaker congratulates nation on Independence Day
item.description: Marlen Mamataliev, Speaker of the Jogorku Kenesh, congratulated Kyrgyzstan's citizens on the 35th anniversary of Independence. He emphasized that strengthening independence is a duty and highlighted the country's progress in economic, state, and international spheres under President Sadyr Japarov. The Speaker wished for peace, unity, and prosperity.

item.title: Kyrgyz State Secretary Links Xi Jinping's Visit to Ancient Monk's Journey
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Secretary Arslan Koichiev drew a historical parallel between Xi Jinping's visit and the 7th-century monk Xuanzang's journey. Koichiev noted Xi's visit to the same location Xuanzang stayed and referenced Xi's article on Kyrgyzstan-China relations, highlighting historical figures who fostered cultural exchange.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Asked US to Lead Anti-Houthi War, Washington Refused
item.description: Saudi Arabia requested the United States to lead a war against the Houthis, but Washington declined. This issue was raised during a meeting between Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Admiral Brad Cooper, head of the US Central Command, on August 14.

item.title: US President Trump Congratulates Kyrgyzstan on Independence Day
item.description: US President Donald Trump sent congratulations to Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov and the people of Kyrgyzstan on their Independence Day. He highlighted the strong relationship built on mutual respect, economic ties, and shared commitment to regional security. The US reaffirms its support for Kyrgyzstan's sovereignty and independence.

item.title: Leaders of Several Countries Congratulate Kyrgyzstan on 35th Independence Anniversary
item.description: Heads of state from Saudi Arabia, Morocco, Belgium, Iran, Pakistan, Egypt, Belarus, Azerbaijan, and Turkey, along with Armenia's Prime Minister, congratulated Kyrgyzstan on its 35th Independence Day. They wished the nation peace and prosperity and President Japarov good health and success. Several leaders expressed eagerness to deepen bilateral cooperation.

item.title: Kazakh President: Kyrgyzstan Has Successfully Developed Since Independence
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev congratulated Kyrgyzstan on its Independence Day, noting its growing authority, evidenced by its UN Security Council election. He highlighted reforms for economic growth and praised the fraternal relations between Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Shanghai Cooperation Organization Celebrates 25 Years, Drives Regional Economic Cooperation
item.description: The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) marks its 25th anniversary, having grown into a major international body with 27 member states and a GDP nearing $30 trillion. The SCO actively promotes trade, energy, transport, and digital economy projects, enhancing regional stability and global governance.

item.title: Chinese President Xi Jinping Arrives in Bishkek for State Visit and SCO Summit
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife were welcomed in Bishkek by Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov. Xi Jinping conveyed greetings to the Kyrgyz people, highlighting the long-standing friendship and stable development of bilateral relations, now at a high level of comprehensive partnership.

item.title: Britain warns companies supplying arms to Ukraine about Russian attack risks
item.description: British government officials have informed defense company leaders about increased threats from the Kremlin against them and their staff. This warning comes as companies supply arms to Ukraine, highlighting potential Russian attack risks.

item.title: US strikes Iran's Larak Island; Iran retaliates against US bases in Jordan
item.description: The US conducted strikes on Iran's Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz, targeting forces preparing to mine the strait. Iran's IRGC claimed to have retaliated by striking two US military bases in Jordan, targeting infrastructure and fighter jets.

item.title: New Taldykorgan-Ust-Kamenogorsk highway shows significant damage after construction
item.description: Activists report significant damage to the new Taldykorgan-Ust-Kamenogorsk highway, including asphalt degradation and foundation issues, less than two years after its completion. The road, built with Chinese loans, cost over 180 billion tenge and has a two-year warranty.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India Elevate Strategic Partnership to New Level
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Uzbekistan on August 29-30 for a state visit. Discussions focused on deepening strategic partnership and multifaceted cooperation. Trade turnover exceeded $1 billion last year, and the number of joint ventures has increased sevenfold.

item.title: Uzbekistan Focuses SCO Summit on Economic Cooperation and Infrastructure
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will attend the SCO summit in Bishkek on August 31-September 1. The summit marks the organization's 25th anniversary and aims to advance economic, transport, and anti-crisis agendas. Leaders from 21 countries, including China, Russia, and India, are expected to participate.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister's State Visit to Uzbekistan Concludes with Signed Agreements
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi concluded his state visit to Uzbekistan on August 29-30. High-level talks focused on deepening strategic partnership and cooperation in trade, energy, health, and other sectors. A significant package of bilateral agreements was signed.
